```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse=TRUE, comment="#>")
library(gAtoms)
```

`gwishart_log_norm()` computes $\log I_G(b, D)$ for the G-Wishart distribution

$$p(K \mid G, b, D) = I_G(b, D)^{-1} |K|^{(b-2)/2}
  \exp\left\{-\tfrac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}(KD)\right\},$$

which is the same parameterization used by `BDgraph::gnorm()`. The shape
parameter must be an integer of at least 3 and `D` must be a symmetric positive
definite matrix whose rows and columns follow the graph vertex order; a matrix
with row and column names is realigned to that order automatically.

The computation uses the prime decomposition of the graph: complete prime
components and clique separators are evaluated with the exact complete-graph
closed form, and only an incomplete prime component is passed to the optional
`BDgraph::gnorm()`.

```{r decomposable}
G <- igraph::set_vertex_attr(igraph::make_ring(4, circular = FALSE),
                             "name", value = c("A", "B", "C", "D"))
dec <- atom_decompose(G)
dec

D <- diag(4)
fit <- gwishart_log_norm(G, b = 3, D = D, decomp = dec)
fit$log_norm
fit$approximate
fit$diagnostics$n_bdgraph_calls
```

Every prime component of this path is complete, so the value is exact and
reported as `approximate = FALSE` with zero BDgraph calls. Supplying `decomp`
reuses the decomposition instead of computing it again.

Per-component contributions and their engine labels are stored for inspection:

```{r contributions}
fit$local_summary
fit$atom_log_norm
fit$separator_log_norm
```

A non-chordal graph has an incomplete prime component. It is handed to
`BDgraph::gnorm()`, and the result is then flagged as approximate because only
that local term is a Monte Carlo estimate:

```{r incomplete-prime, eval=requireNamespace("BDgraph", quietly = TRUE)}
G4 <- igraph::set_vertex_attr(igraph::make_ring(4),
                              "name", value = c("A", "B", "C", "D"))
set.seed(1)
fit4 <- gwishart_log_norm(G4, b = 3, D = diag(4), control = list(iter = 100L))
fit4$approximate
fit4$engine
fit4$diagnostics$n_bdgraph_calls
```

Without BDgraph the closed-form cases above still work; only a graph with an
incomplete prime component requires the optional package.

## Reusing one decomposition across modules

The same `atom_decomp` object can be passed to the companion modules, so the
structural work is done once:

```{r shared-decomposition}
X <- matrix(stats::rnorm(40 * 4), nrow = 40, ncol = 4)
colnames(X) <- c("A", "B", "C", "D")
gfit <- fit_gaussian_graph(X, G, decomp = dec)

dat <- expand.grid(A = c("a", "b"), B = c("a", "b"),
                   C = c("a", "b"), D = c("a", "b"))
dat <- dat[rep(seq_len(nrow(dat)), 1L + (seq_len(nrow(dat)) * 5L) %% 7L), ]
lfit <- fit_loglinear_graph(dat, G, decomp = dec, engine = "loglin")

classes <- c(class(gfit), class(lfit), class(fit))
classes
```

Each module reports its own statistical quantity; only the structural
decomposition is shared.
